title: CFD Investigation of Pitot-Static Tube Performance
summary: Computational fluid dynamics analysis of a nose-cone-mounted pitot-static probe across varying angles of attack at Mach 0.6.

images.caption: Figure 1 - RMIT HIVE rocket launching from Serpentine, Victoria:.
Figure 2 - Internal Pressure Transducer Schema: Overview of pneumatic channel architecture and transducer routing connecting total and static lines to differential pressure sensors (NASA, 2015).

Figure 3 - Angle of Attack Incidence Definition: Geometric definition of vehicle tilt relative to oncoming freestream velocity vectors, governing local streamline curvature and off-axis stagnation point migration.
Figure 4 - Design Methodology Workflow: High-level parametric design and CFD execution pipeline spanning CAD generation in Onshape to ANSYS RANS verification.
Figure 5 - Probe Geometry Dimensions: Dimensioned layout of the 165 mm probe body, wall thickness, and dual axial channel configuration.
Figure 6 - Probe and Nose-Cone Assembly: Dimensioned engineering layout highlighting internal dual-channel routing and mechanical mounting within the RMIT HIVE nose cone.
Figure 7 - Rear Pneumatic Exit Geometry: Detailed view of the 39.4-degree angled rearward outlets sized for flexible line connection to the avionics bay.
Figure 8 - Centring Ring Integration: Mechanical constraint architecture maintaining repeatable alignment along the cone axis under aerodynamic loading.
Figure 9 - Differential Pressure Sensor Module: Integrated avionics hardware module capturing time-resolved pressure differential across total and static lines.
Figure 10 - CAD Multi-View Orthographics: Comprehensive orthographic projection detailing outer diameter, channel lengths, and port positioning.
Figure 11 - Scaled Assembly Drawing: Detailed engineering blueprint showcasing alignment features and boundary constraints.
Figure 12 - Full Domain Velocity Streamlines: Global flow visualization across the 10-meter cubic enclosure domain surrounding the vehicle.
Figure 13 - Multi-Incidence Flow Field Progression: Comparative multi-panel overview showing streamline divergence across increasing angles of attack.
Figure 14 - Wall-Resolved Computational Mesh: Discretized fluid domain emphasizing fine prismatic inflation layers around static ports and stagnation inlet to resolve wall shear stress.
Figure 15 - Far-Field Coarsening Grid: Element-quality distribution showing structured near-body cells with graded coarsening toward outer far-field boundaries.
Figure 16 - Static Port Local Mesh Refinement: High-resolution grid density isolating the 1.0 mm radial static ports for accurate local pressure extraction.
Figure 17 - Turbulence Model Validation Slice: Detailed view of wall-resolved k-omega SST inflation layers ensuring proper y+ compliance.
Figure 18 - Mesh Quality Element Distribution: Element metric evaluation ensuring solution stability and minimal cell skewness throughout the fluid volume.
Figure 19 - Baseline Static-Pressure Contour (M=0.6, alpha=0 degrees): Verification contour showing stagnation core pressure at the pitot inlet and symmetric acceleration along the cone profile.
Figure 20 - Off-Axis Pressure Contour Sweep: Multi-incidence pressure distribution contours demonstrating progressive asymmetry and stagnation point migration.
Figure 21 - Normalised Total-Pressure Error vs. Alpha: Quantitative evaluation showing total-pressure error remaining within the +/- 1% acceptance band strictly up to alpha <= 5 degrees.
Figure 22 - Historical NACA Reference Benchmark Grid: Classical NASA/NACA validation curve defining the +/- 1% insensitivity window for cylindrical pitot geometries across off-axis flow.
